banana: This tropical fruit has a long curved shape and a yellow peel. People remove the peel in strips to eat the soft flesh.
A bunch contains several curved yellow fruits joined at one end. Each fruit has soft pale flesh inside a thick peel.
The snack is a sweet yellow fruit shaped like a crescent. Its skin is peeled downward before the inside is eaten.
These long fruits grow in bunches in warm countries. When ripe, their yellow skins develop brown spots and their flesh is soft.
A yellow fruit bends in a curve and has no hard central core. Its thick skin can be pulled off in long strips by hand.
The fruit is long and curved, with creamy pale flesh. It hangs in a bunch and changes from green to yellow as it ripens.
apple: This round fruit grows on orchard trees and may have red or green skin. It has crunchy flesh and a seed-filled core.
The fruit is firm and round, with a small stalk at the top. It is commonly pressed into cider and baked in pies.
A red-skinned orchard fruit makes a crisp crunch when bitten. Several small brown seeds sit inside its central core.
These round fruits grow on trees in temperate orchards. Their skin can be green, red, or yellow, and their center contains a hard seeded core.
The cook cuts a round green fruit into wedges and removes the core. Its crisp white flesh is used for a cinnamon pie.
A shiny red fruit has crunchy white flesh under its thin skin. The seeds are grouped in a core at the center.
elephant: This huge land animal has a long flexible trunk and two ivory tusks. Its large ears spread out on either side of its head.
The gray mammal picks up food with a trunk instead of using its mouth directly. It has thick legs, a massive body, and large ears.
A very large African animal sprays water over its back using its long trunk. Curved ivory tusks grow beside the trunk.
This enormous herbivore has broad ears and four thick legs. Its nose forms a long trunk that can grasp branches.
The zoo animal has wrinkled gray skin, a long trunk, and ivory tusks. It uses the tip of its trunk to lift small pieces of food.
A herd of huge gray mammals walks with their calves. The adults have long trunks and broad ears, and some have large white tusks.
giraffe: This African animal has an exceptionally long neck and a spotted coat. It reaches leaves high in trees while standing on four long legs.
The tallest living land animal has brown patches on a pale body. Its very long neck lets it eat leaves above other animals.
A tall spotted animal stretches its long neck to reach an acacia tree. Two small horn-like knobs stand on top of its head.
This zoo mammal has a very long neck, long thin legs, and a patchy brown coat. Its head rises far above a nearby person.
The animal's neck is much longer than those of other hoofed mammals. It has a spotted coat and feeds on leaves in tall African trees.
A very tall African herbivore has a long dark tongue and a long neck. Brown patches cover its body, and small horn-like knobs sit above its ears.
piano: This large musical instrument has 88 black and white keys. Pressing the keys makes internal hammers hit strings, and foot pedals control the sound.
A musician sits at a bench to play this instrument with both hands. Its long keyboard has black and white keys and pedals beneath it.
The instrument has a wide keyboard, strings inside a wooden case, and felt-covered hammers. It is made in grand and upright forms.
This acoustic keyboard instrument has 88 keys and a heavy wooden body. A player presses a pedal to let the notes continue ringing.
The concert instrument has black and white keys at the front and strings under a large lid. The performer sits down and plays the keys with both hands.
An upright musical instrument stands against a wall with a bench in front. Its black and white keys move hammers that strike strings inside.
violin: This small wooden instrument has four strings and is held under the chin. A musician draws a bow across its strings to play it.
The player rests a small string instrument on the shoulder and beneath the chin. It has four tuning pegs and is normally played with a bow.
A high-pitched orchestral string instrument has four strings and a chinrest. The musician holds it under the jaw while moving a horsehair bow.
This small bowed instrument is the highest standard member of the orchestral string family. It has four strings and is held between the chin and shoulder.
The instrument has a small wooden body, four strings, and a carved scroll. A shoulder rest supports it while the player bows the strings beneath the chin.
A musician tucks this four-stringed instrument under the chin. One hand presses the strings along its neck while the other moves a bow.
